title: GradReason: LLMs as Meta-Learners that Replace Training Epochs with Training-Data-Free Weight Updates
read_level: full (pdftotext of v1, two-column layout interleaved; references skimmed)
why_wsp: Every ten epochs an LLM agent inspects a training run's weight snapshots and epoch gradients in a sandbox and writes a Python program that computes new weights ("virtual epochs") with no gradient on training data, gated by a validation check.
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5 (adaptive thinking, medium effort)
interface: code/tensor tools (sandboxed Python analysis + submitted update program; autodiff disabled)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (invoked every 10 epochs; validation acceptance rule; outcomes of previous window fed back)
self_editing: no; the LLM edits a separate network being trained
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: all parameters replaced per accepted virtual epoch (mostly snapshot averages); "Of its 301 accepted virtual epochs, 284 were averages" (Sec 6.2)

headline_results.claim: Opus saved 32.8% data epochs at 0.31pp lower accuracy
headline_results.quote: Claude Opus 5.5 used 32.8% fewer data epochs than the 80-epoch recipe at 0.31 percentage points lower test accuracy (95% CI −0.72 to +0.09; 0.94 points on ResNet-18)
Against the frontier at the same number of data epochs, Opus was 0.18 pp more accurate (95% CI −0.18 to +0.54; 7 wins, 5 losses; p = 0.52)

headline_results.claim: Controls: a-priori rule 5.4%, rule with averaging 25.0%
headline_results.quote: a fixed rule with the same acceptance check but extrapolations from prior work saved 5.4% of the data epochs, and the same rule with averaging added saved 25.0%

headline_results.claim: Opus chose snapshot averaging in every run, unprompted
headline_results.quote: Unprompted, Opus averaged recent weight snapshots in every run.
The median accepted virtual epoch of Sonnet moved the weights by 0.5% of the distance a data epoch covered at the same point of training, against 73% for Opus.
Opus saved 12.5 pp more of the data epochs than Sonnet (95% CI 2.8 to 22.2; 11 wins in 12; Wilcoxon p = 0.011)

headline_results.claim: GPU time saved smaller than data epochs saved
headline_results.quote: Opus saved 22.5% of the GPU time of the 80-epoch recipe (standard deviation 8.8), the rule 19.6% and Sonnet 12.1%

cost.quote: An Opus run cost 0.68 USD in API fees (standard deviation 0.10) and a Sonnet run 0.89 USD
The 24 agent runs of the main study cost 18.92 USD over 694 API calls
Counting this latency, an Opus run took 39% longer than the 80-epoch recipe and a Sonnet run 174% longer.
wrote 2,353 output tokens per invocation, thinking included. Sonnet needed 5.71 requests on average ... and 7,164 output tokens

baselines_and_controls: standard recipe at budgets 10/20/30/40/60/80 epochs (frontier, each with own cosine schedule); a-priori rule (Leap+Verify-style extrapolations, same machinery); hand-designed rule encoding the agents' averaging; Opus vs Sonnet
runs_and_variance: 120 runs: 72 recipe + 12 each for two rules, Opus, Sonnet; 2 seeds x 6 settings; s.d., 95% t intervals, Wilcoxon and sign tests reported; "With 12 pairs these tests detect only large effects, and we treat them as indicative" (Sec 5)
robustness_of_edits: not tested beyond held-out test accuracy; averaging gains vanish after next data epoch: "The gain was gone after the next data epoch at the high learning rate" (Sec 6.2)
verification: statistical acceptance rule on 5,000 held-out validation images (accuracy within 0.3pp, loss within 1%); static checks and sandbox; no formal verification
memorization_vs_reasoning: Averaging is a known technique (SWA/LAWA); authors describe it as "an unprompted choice of a known technique, not as an invention"; example rationale "often helps" shows choice "drew on prior knowledge as well as on the measurements" (App A); Sonnet averaged in only 1 of 12 runs; pilot prompt may have mentioned averaging.
limitations_stated: Small evaluation (3 small architectures, 2 CIFAR datasets, 2 seeds, one provider); latency exceeds GPU savings at this scale; acceptance rule admits near-identity updates and cumulative drift; not data-free (uses validation set); restricted interpreter is not a security boundary; nondeterministic LLM decisions; pilot prompt may have influenced averaging.
code_or_data: "will be made publicly available upon publication" (Data availability); none found
notes_for_survey: LLM writes weight-update programs inside a training run, not edits of a trained network; strong budget-matched baselines show savings lie on the recipe's own data/accuracy frontier and are reproducible by a fixed rule once the agent's choice (snapshot averaging) is known. Includes near-identity-update failure mode where acceptance checks are gamed by no-op updates (Sonnet).
